summary_paragraph: A woman with brittle type 1 diabetes, recurrent gastroparesis, chronic kidney disease stage II, and a history of anxiety and depression was readmitted within 24 hours of discharge due to persistent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. Her symptoms were exacerbated by uncontrolled diabetes and possible gastroesophageal reflux. Chest tightness was evaluated with a normal chest X-ray, ruling out acute cardiopulmonary causes. She was managed with IV fluids, insulin adjustment to her home NPH regimen, and anti-nausea medications while avoiding contraindicated drugs due to allergies. She gradually advanced to a soft diet, with improvement in symptoms and stable renal function. Omeprazole was continued for acid suppression. A coordinated discharge plan included follow-up with her primary care provider, mental health support, and ophthalmology for background diabetic retinopathy. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for ongoing diabetes and gastroparesis management.
